stories.title: Police use facial recognition to scan one million faces in WA trial leading to 122 arrests
stories.summary: The story title says a Western Australian facial-recognition trial scanned one million faces and led to 122 arrests, but the attached Guardian link covers a different subject. That report says 55% of Victorian lawyers now use AI, up from 37% the previous year, while only a quarter have reduced client fees as a result.

stories.title: Experts warn AI copyright changes could breach Australian constitution and spark huge compensation rights case
stories.summary: The story title says experts warn proposed AI copyright changes could breach Australia’s constitution and trigger a major compensation-rights case. The attached Guardian report says artists in Anthony Albanese’s Grayndler electorate are opposing potential copyright changes affecting AI, creating disquiet in the prime minister’s normally safe inner-Sydney seat.

stories.title: Labor and the Coalition are poised to take a reckless gamble on AI. Haven’t they realised community support has collapsed? | Edward Santow and Sarah Sacher
stories.summary: Edward Santow and Sarah Sacher argue that Labor and the Coalition are moving toward a reckless consensus on artificial intelligence despite declining community support. They say Australian workers expect government protection from AI harms and that a clear reform option is available.
